title: In a dystopian London where emotions are digitized, this hand-drawn ink art is the only piece of human reality left. First sketch for FLATLINE's upcoming Pilot.
author: KDH_Studio_Official
selftext:
Hey everyone!

If you’ve played the current demo for my psychological interactive movie FLATLINE: Pay to Feel, you’ve seen a world built entirely on a heavily stylized, tech-driven visual language (AI-processed real footage of London). 

This was a deliberate choice to match the main character’s profession. He is an engineer, and he perceives his environment through a cold, analytical, and digital lens.

But I realized that this look only tells half the story. The narrative desperately needs a counterweight—another perspective on this sterile world.

For the upcoming Pilot episode, I am introducing a hybrid visual style. While the core game remains an interactive movie made from real London footage with digital processing, I am weaving in raw, hand-drawn ink art. These analog pieces will represent the fading memories and the viewpoint of a creative person trying to communicate from within this emotionless reality.

This ink pen drawing is the very first sketch for these memory elements. The full Pilot will feature a deep contrast between the digital, generated environments and these sharp, physical strokes of human art.

I’d love to hear your thoughts on this direction! You can check out the tech-driven perspective in the current demo on Steam here:

 https://store.steampowered.com/app/4711800/FLATLINE\_Pay\_to\_Feel/?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=social

comments.author: Electronic-Pool-7458
comments.body:
I like the art a lot. 

If the idea is for the second perspective to be the more emotional one, how do you think it would look if you added boiling lines, for example? 

It might reinforce the feeling of something subjective and a bit volatile.

replies.author: KDH_Studio_Official
replies.body:
Thanks for the great feedback! 
I really love the concept of line boil to reinforce that subjective, volatile feeling. Since it's an interactive movie, adding that subtle organic movement to the drawings could bridge the gap between video and art nicely. 
Appreciate the suggestion!

comments.author: SanoKei
comments.body: I read that as "emotions are dignified" and I was thinking "well I do know Londoners but... OH"

replies.author: KDH_Studio_Official
replies.body: Haha, well, standard Londoners already have that 'dystopian emotionless' vibe down perfectly, so you weren't completely wrong!
